summary: The nex-controller Debian package and Controller appliance builders now install gcc and libc6-dev and export CGO_ENABLED=1 before go build, so the packaged Controller links the real go-sqlite3 driver instead of the CGO-disabled stub that cannot open its database. API impact: none.

guide.reason: Build-time toolchain fix. The documented install, upgrade and appliance workflows are unchanged; a working package now behaves as the guide already describes.

api.reason: Only how the Controller binary is compiled changes. No Controller-Core operation, agent command, client endpoint or result flow is added or altered.

roadmap.reason: Defect fix from the Phase 2 gate; no milestone changes.

state.reason: No durable state is added or moved; the Controller keeps its existing database, which this fix makes openable again.

verification.method: Added ControllerCgoBuildTests to tests/test_distribution_packaging.py; it failed before the fix (packaging/controller/Dockerfile lacked gcc and libc6-dev, neither build script exported CGO_ENABLED=1) and passes after. Built a throwaway 0.2.10~cgocheck nex-controller package from a freshly generated source bundle with packaging/controller/build.py in Docker, extracted the binary, confirmed go version -m reports CGO_ENABLED=1, and started it on 127.0.0.1 with an empty data directory and temporary TLS files: it created controller.db, logged listening and answered HTTPS 200 with no go-sqlite3 stub error. The appliance image was not rebuilt; its Dockerfile already installed gcc and libc6-dev. No lab, host install or apt upgrade was exercised.
